items.title: Galbot Prices ET1 Humanoid From 79,000 Yuan Across Three Versions
items.summary: Galbot has priced its ET1 bipedal humanoid in three versions, starting at 79,000 yuan. The Standard version is 79,000 yuan, the Pro is 139,000 yuan, and the Flagship is 179,000 yuan. The Pro tier includes "watch-and-learn" capabilities, while the Flagship offers more onboard compute and development options. These tiers differentiate features such as interactive learning, dynamic reasoning, and the inclusion of dexterous hands. The pricing establishes the cost for different levels of performance and advanced functionality in the humanoid robot.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, Galbot prices the ET1 Humanoid from 79,000 Yuan across three distinct versions. The available versions include the Standard at 79,000 Yuan, the Pro model priced at 139,000 Yuan, and the Flagship version set at 179,000 Yuan. The Pro tier incorporates watch-and-learn capabilities, while the Flagship tier introduces enhanced onboard compute and additional development options. These tiers differentiate features such as interactive learning, dynamic reasoning, and the inclusion of dexterous hands, reflecting varying levels of performance and advanced functionality in the robot. This pricing strategy indicates a segmentation of the humanoid market based on advanced AI capabilities and physical dexterity. The development of these tiered systems signals increasing market segmentation in advanced robotics.

items.title: Boston Dynamics Gives Atlas Four-Finger Hands Built for Tools and AI Training
items.summary: Boston Dynamics introduced new four-finger hands for Atlas, increasing the degrees of freedom from seven to thirteen. These hands feature direct actuation and tactile sensors to enable object manipulation and tool operation. The design prioritizes dexterity, strength, and manufacturability, resulting in a hand size comparable to a human hand. The four-finger configuration allows for in-hand reorientation and gripping of tools. Engineers deliberately omitted a fifth finger to manage cost and potential failure points.

This development signals a step forward in enabling more sophisticated physical tasks for artificial intelligence systems.

items.title: Your Robot’s Safety Functions Already Work. What If the Input Lies?
items.summary: Robot safety functions rely on inputs like distance readings or stop signals, which can be deliberately manipulated to cause unintended behavior. Research shows that adversarial inputs, such as altered images or audio, can change a robot's actions despite protective systems being in place. This manipulation challenges safety assessments that often only consider accidental faults, necessitating a focus on deliberate cyber attacks. Safety teams must investigate the source and integrity of all information used by safeguards to ensure they remain effective. Strengthening safety requires testing against manipulated inputs and continuously updating evidence throughout the robot's lifecycle.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, "Your Robot’s Safety Functions Already Work. What If the Input Lies?". This story examines how robot safety functions can be compromised through manipulated input data. Research indicates that adversarial inputs, such as altered images or audio, can cause robots to change their actions even when protective systems are active. The methodology involved demonstrating that intentional manipulation of distance readings or stop signals can lead to unintended robotic behavior. This challenges existing safety assessments which typically focus only on accidental faults, underscoring the need to account for deliberate cyber attacks. Safety teams must now investigate the source and integrity of all information used by safeguards to ensure their continued effectiveness. Strengthening safety requires testing against manipulated inputs and continuously updating evidence throughout the robot's lifecycle. The industry must prioritize testing against malicious inputs and establishing continuous monitoring protocols for data integrity.

items.title: Musk Says Tesla Halved AI5 RAM to Secure Memory for Optimus Production
items.summary: Elon Musk stated that Tesla halved the RAM allocation for AI5 to 72GB and reduced AI6's by one-third to 144GB to accommodate Optimus production. This change was implemented to reduce costs while keeping memory bandwidth unchanged. Musk expects these reductions to have a negligible impact on Optimus performance because memory bandwidth is the primary constraint. This adjustment is intended to improve component supply and lower costs for scaling humanoid robot production. The update reflects a supply constraint in achieving the company's humanoid ambitions.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, "Musk Says Tesla Halved AI5 RAM to Secure Memory for Optimus Production". This segment reports on Tesla's adjustments to memory allocation for AI systems to support the production of the Optimus humanoid robot. Tesla has halved the RAM allocation for AI5 to seventy-two gigabytes and reduced the allocation for AI6 by one-third to one hundred forty-four gigabytes. This adjustment was implemented to accommodate the demands of Optimus production while maintaining memory bandwidth levels. The rationale behind the changes was to reduce operational costs and improve the supply chain for components necessary for scaling humanoid robot manufacturing. The update indicates a supply constraint is currently impacting the company's humanoid production goals. This development signals ongoing optimization efforts within the technology sector concerning advanced AI hardware scaling.

items.title: Nucleus Shares Nearly Two Hours of Factory Work, Says Demo Is 60% Autonomous
items.summary: Melvin Schwarz described nearly two hours of factory work from Nucleus, showing visible interventions. The demonstration featured a 60% autonomous and 40% teleoperated operation. Nucleus now regularly conducts four-to-six-hour shifts, combining autonomy with human assistance in industrial deployments. The company's approach involves supervised operation and interventions to gather training data before achieving full autonomy. This demonstration provides context for understanding the balance between human and robot involvement in industrial tasks.

items.title: UBTECH CEO Tours Robot Factory, Says Monthly Output Could Reach 1,500 Units
items.summary: CEO James Zhou toured UBTECH's factory, detailing production capacity for humanoid robots. The 14,000-square-meter facility can potentially produce a humanoid every eight to ten minutes at maximum capacity. Monthly output is estimated to reach approximately 1,500 units based on these figures. The factory incorporates human-robot collaboration for material handling, with robots managing packaging and transport alongside workers. Furthermore, an automated vertical warehouse can store 112 humanoid robots within a small footprint.

items.title: Atlas Robot’s New Hand May Outperform Humanlike Designs
items.summary: Boston Dynamics has redesigned the Atlas robot's hand to prioritize real-world applicability over purely humanlike aesthetics. The new design focuses on achieving a balance of capability, ruggedness, manufacturability, and low cost. This involves simplifying the design, such as removing the pinky, and increasing the degrees of freedom from seven to thirteen. The new hand is engineered to be strong, capable of using tools, and easily mass-produced and repaired. This approach suggests that scaling humanoid robots will require making design trade-offs for practicality.

Boston Dynamics implemented this redesign by simplifying the design, specifically removing the pinky, and increasing the degrees of freedom from seven to thirteen. This modification was engineered to enhance the hand's strength, enabling the use of tools, and to ensure the mechanism is easily mass-produced and repaired through a practical engineering approach. This strategy indicates that scaling humanoid robots necessitates making deliberate design trade-offs for practical functionality. The industry should observe further developments in practical robotics design and scalable physical interaction.

items.title: Precision In Motion. Vishay Precision Group, Inc. (VPG) to Showcase Custom Sensing Capabilities for Humanoid Robotics at RoboBusiness 2026
items.summary: Vishay Precision Group (VPG) will showcase custom force and torque sensing solutions for humanoid robotics at RoboBusiness 2026. These sensors are crucial because humanoid robots require precise, real-time feedback for safe and smooth interaction with unpredictable environments. VPG designs custom strain gage-based sensors built directly into robot structures to measure forces, torques, and multi-axis data. Specific solutions include miniature tactile sensors for fingertips, multi-axis sensors for joints, and joint torque sensors for actuators. VPG also offers complete engineering support to help move robotic designs from concept to large-scale production.

items.title: Robot Talk Episode 164 – Accelerating robot learning, with Michelle Lu
items.summary: Claire interviewed Michelle Lu of Vsim Technology about using simulation and artificial intelligence to teach robots new skills. Lu previously co-founded Isaac Gym, a framework for GPU-accelerated reinforcement learning in robotics. Vsim was established to address limitations in simulation-based robotics AI concerning efficiency, scalability, and the sim-to-real gap. The Robot Talk podcast explores the field of robotics, artificial intelligence, and autonomous machines. This episode focuses on advancing robot learning through simulation and AI methods.

items.title: Bounded-Fidelity Sim-as-Demo-Stage: Mocap Handoff for Governance Benchmarks
items.summary: The research addresses the issue of contact force integration noise in simulators, which creates divergence in audit-chain logs for LLM-driven robots during object handoffs. The authors propose bounded-fidelity sim-as-demo-stage, a pattern that suppresses contact physics within defined handoff envelopes while maintaining full dynamics elsewhere. This method uses a MuJoCo mocap primitive driven by a Python adapter to achieve this control over simulation fidelity. Experiments show that by controlling envelope-edge timing jitter, audit chain reproducibility is achieved with near-zero engineering cost. This pattern allows benchmark designers to ensure audit-chain stability in simulations without incurring high fidelity costs.

items.title: Multi-Reference Path Tracking Control for an Agricultural Tractor with Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
items.summary: A path tracking controller based on Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) is developed for guiding agricultural tractors along a predefined path. The NMPC objective function incorporates multiple segments of a piecewise-linear reference path. Methods are also presented for selecting the most viable reference segments from the full path. Field tests demonstrated that the NMPC solver converged quickly and achieved a mean absolute cross-track error of 6.1 cm while tracking the curved path.

items.title: Probabilistic Plan Legibility with Off-the-shelf Planners
items.summary: The paper proposes a method for legible planning in arbitrary PDDL domains by extending prior research on planning legibility. It avoids the need to construct ad-hoc planners by focusing on planning with off-the-shelf planners. The method incorporates a second-order theory of mind to estimate the observer's perspective, which helps in understanding goal disambiguation. Legibility is shown to be a trade-off with plan efficiency, requiring a regularizing factor for optimal balance. This approach has potential applications in human-robot teaming scenarios.

items.title: HumanoidTTT: Test-Time Capability Reuse for Efficient Humanoid Control
items.summary: HumanoidTTT is a framework designed for test-time capability reuse in continual humanoid control to improve efficiency. It introduces Selective Full-Motion Reuse to allow direct reuse of complete motions from certified entry states, bypassing fresh generation. Test-Time Capability Consolidation adapts which qualified capabilities are retained in a store based on subsequent deployment reuse feedback. Experiments showed zero unsafe accepts and a 16.4$\times$ speedup over fresh generation. This method also improved avoided generator calls by 13.2 per 200 requests compared to a frozen counterpart.

items.title: Real-Time Whole-Body Safe Motion Generation for Multi-Segment Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots
items.summary: The paper proposes a unified actuation-space framework for real-time, safe motion generation in multi-segment tendon-driven continuum robots. It utilizes an energy-based variable-curvature model to account for non-uniform bending and provides analytical Jacobians for kinematic calculations. A multipoint Control Barrier Function-Quadratic Programming (CBF-QP) enforces backbone clearance and respects actuation limits to ensure collision avoidance. Experiments showed a 96% collision-free success rate in static scenarios and 100% in dynamic ones, demonstrating real-time performance of 6.66 ms.

items.title: DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies
items.summary: DriftOPD is a teacher-free, rollout-free framework for sequence-level on-policy distillation of continuous Vision-Language-Action (VLA) action experts. It decomposes the sequence-level reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence into a chunk-level term and a future-potential term reflecting long-horizon effects. The framework optimizes these terms using a one-step drifting objective and a Q-function critic learned from offline demonstrations. This allows for sequence-level optimization using only offline data and one-step action generation. DriftOPD achieves performance comparable to multi-step teacher policies in various VLA architectures.

items.title: IndoorBEV: A Lightweight Real-Time LiDAR BEV Perception System for Indoor Mobile Robots
items.summary: IndoorBEV is a lightweight framework for real-time LiDAR perception in indoor mobile robots by using a height-aware Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) representation. It mitigates the loss of vertical geometric information by summarizing vertical point distribution using statistical height features and multi-frequency height encoding. The system employs a lightweight encoder to integrate geometric and local features to produce semantic BEV maps and object bounding boxes. IndoorBEV has a small parameter count of 0.6M and achieves low latency of 169.6 ms on target hardware. Evaluations confirm a favorable balance between perception accuracy, speed, and memory consumption.

items.title: DexPolicy: Scheduled Exploration for Trajectory-Guided Dexterous Manipulation
items.summary: DexPolicy introduces scheduled exploration to guide trajectory-guided dexterous manipulation by explicitly controlling the exploration scale during training. It anneals the exploration from broad to narrow as training progresses while keeping other parameters fixed. Experiments across different policy-optimization settings, including PPO, GRPO, and FPO, showed improvements in deterministic target success. Specifically, the FPO method achieved a higher mean target success than linear decay in some evaluations. The study concludes that schedules should be judged by terminal task success under intended execution conditions.
